chapter: Film work, recording and looking back
title: His first recordings and the Ory radio date
summary: Blakeney discusses recordings from 1925, the gap to 1947, the unknowing KHJ broadcast with Ory, and the 1961 Verve session.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Mr. Blakeney, as far as your recording experiences were, what do

you remember as your most--you feel--your most significant performance; when you think you played best? You mentioned that in your earlier life you didn't receive the recognition--that you were playing very well but you did not receive the popular recognition that often happens to musicians. You had a very, very long span when you did no recordings.
Your first recordings were made, I believe, around--well you tell me, with Reb Spikes.
The first recording was around 1925 when I first came to California.
Then you also did some more recording, and I will give a complete discography at the end of this interview, with Sonny Clay in 1925; is that correct?
Yes.
There was a span from 1925 until 1947 where we have no recordings;
perhaps there were some done but we have no record of them. The first was This Is Jazz.
That was done with Kid Ory?
That was done with Kid Ory.
Do you want to tell us something about that record date?
That was done at old KHJ radio station and we had an audience. I didn't know it was going to be recorded, but it was.
You didn't know you were coming for a record date?
No, I didn't know it was going to be a recording; to me it was just a concert.
That's the thing again, recording and the musicians don't even know what's going on.
On that date was Joe Darensbourg--everybody was the same except it wasn't Barney Bigard.
Was that on Circle label?
Yes.
So it was a broadcast at KHJ?
KHJ.
You also did some recordings later on with Kid Ory in 1961.
That was on the Verve label.
As I said before, would you like to comment on any of your records that you made during your lifetime? What you think was your best, did you have any compositions of your own?
My playing, according to my own opinion, was with Kid Ory on Verve.
That was in 1961?
1961. The rest of them weren't actually recordings, somebody took off and made a record of it on their own and later on off a radio broadcast and later on somebody made an LP out of it.
